Select Similar – Angle

Select faces with a similar orientation, even across disconnected parts of an architectural or geometric mesh.

Cinema 4D 2026PythonPolygon selection

The task

Selecting faces one by one was slowing down my modelling. I wanted the principle of Blender’s Select Similar → Normal directly in Cinema 4D, without switching applications.

The approach

I developed this Python script with AI assistance, specifying the controls I actually needed: a reference selection, an angle tolerance and a way to restore the starting point. The floating window stays open while I work in the viewport.

In use

Tested in Cinema 4D 2026 in my own workflow. It lets me repeat the selection and try different tolerances without returning to Blender.

Controls

  • Angle slider from 0 to 180°.
  • Capture the selection to keep a set of reference faces.
  • Apply different tolerances against those references.
  • Restore the original visible selection.
  • Optionally include opposite normals.

Workflow

  1. Choose the English or French script below, open it in Cinema 4D’s Script Manager and run it.
  2. Choose an editable polygon object, switch to Polygon mode and select reference faces.
  3. In the English version, click “Capture reference selection”.
  4. Set the angle, optionally include opposite normals, then click “Apply selection”.
  5. Adjust and apply again, or use “Restore reference selection” to return to the starting faces.

Scope & limitations

Works on the active polygon object, using geometric normals in object-local space. Hidden faces keep their selection state. Phong normals and deformations are not evaluated; n-gons use Cinema 4D’s internal triangles and quads. After a topology change, capture the references again. Ctrl+Z undoes the selection.

Original French version tested by the author in Cinema 4D 2026. The English version translates the interface and messages, with the same selection logic. Other Cinema 4D versions have not been verified.
